recognition.note: 157 UN members recognise the State of Palestine in the atlas dataset (Wikipedia list, 23 Sep 2025), after the May 2024 trio (Ireland, Norway, Spain) and the September 2025 wave (UK, Canada, Australia, Portugal, France and others at the UN summit). Israel and the United States do not; Palestine is a non-member observer state of the UN since 2012. This card describes the State of Palestine / PLO / Palestinian Authority under Abbas in Ramallah; Hamas in Gaza is a separate actor (nsa-hamas).

stances_toward.note: Belgium announced on 2 Sep 2025 that it would recognise Palestine at the UN General Assembly and signed the New York Declaration, but the formal recognition by royal decree was made conditional on the release of the last hostage and the exclusion of Hamas from government; De Wever added that diplomatic relations would follow only after Hamas's demilitarisation and elections. As of the sources found (Jan 2026 pressure from Vooruit; no decree reported by Oct 2026) the act is not signed, which is why the recognition dataset still shows non-recognition. Grade is our reading of an announced but unformalised recognition (C). Warming. Bond none.

stances_toward.note: Partner and patron rather than ally: Egypt recognised Palestine in 1988, wrote the Gaza reconstruction plan (about USD 53bn, five years, a technocratic committee) that the Arab League adopted on 4 Mar 2025, co-chaired the Sharm el-Sheikh summit of 13 Oct 2025 and hosts Palestinian talks, police training and the Rafah crossing. Its interest is its own as much as Palestinian: the Sinai displacement red line and control of who governs Gaza. The International Stabilization Force question is open: Egypt is not among the five troop contributors named in Feb 2026, wants a 10,000-strong Palestinian force, and its role is border security and training. Bond kin (language, religion, the Sinai-Gaza border).

stances_toward.note: Kin and custodian, but partner rather than ally: Jordan recognised Palestine in 1988 (dataset row), has a population that is an estimated 55-70% of Palestinian origin (CRS), trains Palestinian police at JIPTC and supplies Gaza through the Allenby corridor, and the King repeats a two-state solution with East Jerusalem as the capital. The structural limit is that Jordan's first red line is that the Palestinian question not be settled on its territory: it refused Trump's displacement idea on 11 Feb 2025 (offering only 2,000 sick children), rejects confederation or a security 'substitute' role in the West Bank, and its interest in Palestinian statehood is also its interest in keeping Palestinians out. Bond - kin: language, religion, demography, the 1948-67 history.

stances_toward.note: The state works with the Palestinian Authority to disarm the camps: a joint presidential declaration of Aoun and Abbas on 21 May 2025, and Fatah's handovers of weapons to the army from August 2025 (Burj al-Barajneh, the Tyre camps, then Ain al-Hilweh's last heavy weapons in December 2025). Hamas has refused, and Lebanon's state still hosts the refugees without citizenship. Partner with the PA, not with the camps' other factions; bond affinity (Arab solidarity); confidence C since the PA does not control the camps.

stances_toward.note: Latvia has not recognised a Palestinian state and says it will not for now: recognition should come through a negotiated two-state agreement endorsed by the UN Security Council, and the Foreign Ministry restated this in September 2025 while the UK, Canada and Australia recognised. Contacts exist at working level (a special representative to Palestine, based in Riga, since 2014; Foreign Minister Braze met her Palestinian counterpart on 28 Aug 2025 and called for the hostages' release, a ceasefire and aid). Neutral because Riga neither opposes nor backs the Palestinian claim. Bond - none.

stances_toward.note: Rival, not adversary: Hamas does not seek the Palestinian Authority's destruction, it seeks to displace it inside the PLO. The 2007 split (Hamas expelled Fatah from Gaza after winning the 2006 election) has never been mended: the Beijing Declaration of 23 Jul 2024 (14 factions, a transitional unity government) produced no government, relations in Aug 2026 are described as hostile, Fatah tried to head off a Hamas-Dahlan opposition bloc, Abbas called the Oct 2025 executions a crime (index source) and on 10 Oct 2026 he postponed the legislative vote to 11 Sep 2027. PCPSR's Aug 2026 poll shows Hamas losing support. Bond: grievance (the 2007 coup and the executions), although kin by nation.

stances_toward.note: Oman recognised the State of Palestine in 1988; there is a Palestinian embassy in Muscat and the foreign ministry held in Oct 2023 that Israeli occupation is illegal and called for an independent state and an impartial probe in Gaza. Its stated condition for any normalisation with Israel is a sovereign Palestinian state. The reading rests on the Arab Center DC article (the Palestinian bar to normalisation) and the foreign ministry statements cited by Wikipedia; hence C. Bond affinity: the cause, with the historical wrinkle that the PLO backed the Dhofar rebels.

Warming on that vote; the humanitarian line is children from Gaza treated in Romanian hospitals (Dan, Feb 2026). Bond - none.

stances_toward.note: Slovenia recognised the State of Palestine and established diplomatic relations on 4-5 Jun 2024 and, on the Security Council, voted for Palestine's full UN membership and co-sponsored the General Assembly resolution (143-9-25). Cooling since June 2026: the Janša government, which opposed the recognition, took the Palestinian flag off the government building and lifted the Israel measures. The recognition itself is not reversed in any source found.

relations_to.summary: Belgium announced on 2 Sep 2025 that it would recognise Palestine at the UN General Assembly and signed the New York Declaration; the formal recognition by royal decree is conditional on the release of the last hostage and the exclusion of Hamas from governing Palestine, with diplomatic relations only after demilitarisation and elections. No decree reported by Oct 2026 (the recognition dataset still carries a non-recognition row); a Jul 2026 report that Belgium began drafting the procedure rests on a single Azerbaijani outlet.

relations_to.summary: At the UN General Assembly in September 2025 Stubb met President Abbas, said Israel has no right to violate international law in Palestine and that the 1967 occupation must end, and said he would accept recognition of Palestine immediately if the government proposed it; the government has not proposed it because the Finns Party and the Christian Democrats object. Finland had joined a declaration on a two-state solution.

relations_to.summary: Italy does not recognise Palestine yet: Meloni told the UN (Sept 2025) that Italy would recognise once the hostages are freed and Hamas is excluded from government; Tajani repeated on 29 Jul 2026 that Italy is in favour but only once a state exists, Hamas is disarmed and Israel can recognise it too, and rejects 'demagogic or fictitious' recognition. The non-recognition itself is in the recognition dataset.

relations_to.summary: Jordan wants a two-state outcome with East Jerusalem as the Palestinian capital and refuses the transfer of Gazans or West Bankers into Jordan; the King repeated that position at the White House on 11 Feb 2025 while offering to treat 2,000 sick Gaza children. Jordan also trains Palestinian police (JIPTC) and endorsed UNSC resolution 2803 of 17 Nov 2025 but ruled out joining the International Stabilization Force.

relations_to.summary: Humanitarian cargo to Gaza runs through Jordan under the Jordan Hashemite Charity Organisation and the army (convoys and airdrops, including the UK-backed airdrops of 2024); UNSC resolution 2803 of 17 Nov 2025 was endorsed by Jordan, which declined to send troops to the International Stabilization Force.
